ns1:channel.ns1:title: Nature Reviews Cardiology
ns1:channel.ns1:description: Nature Reviews Cardiology is a peer-reviewed journal for cardiologists and affiliated health-care professionals. The journal delivers timely interpretations of key scientific developments in cardiology and related areas of study. Nature Reviews Cardiology is published monthly in print and online, and includes commissioned news, commentary and opinion pieces, and comprehensive reviews. Articles are subject to rigorous peer-review and/or review by in-house editors. Topics covered include acute coronary syndromes, arrhythmias, angina, cardiomyopathy, concomitant disease, congenital conditions, coronary artery disease, heart failure, hypertension, imaging and other investigations, infection, interventional cardiology, pathology, stroke, surgery, thrombosis, transplantation, valvular disease and vascular disease, as well as general therapies, disease markers, genetics and public health.

ns1:item.ns1:title: Duration of antibiotic treatment for infective endocarditis: should we move towards tailored therapy?
ns1:item.ns5:encoded:
Nature Reviews Cardiology, Published online: 15 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41569-026-01360-1

The POET II trial reports that stopping antibiotic treatment in patients with endocarditis once they are clinically stable shortens the treatment duration without excess risk of death or surgery, but triples the rates of relapse of endocarditis or bacteraemia. This response-guided strategy marks a genuine shift beyond the oral-antibiotic-switch paradigm from the POET trial, and the safety of the approach will depend on rigorous patient selection and close multidisciplinary follow-up.
ns1:item.dc:title: Duration of antibiotic treatment for infective endocarditis: should we move towards tailored therapy?
ns1:item.dc:creator: Mary Philip
Gilbert Habib

ns1:item.ns1:title: Heart-specific T cell responses: from antigens to disease mechanisms
ns1:item.ns5:encoded:
Nature Reviews Cardiology, Published online: 12 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41569-026-01356-x

In this Review, Gustavo Campos Ramos revisits the molecular composition of the heart from a T cell perspective and describes the most relevant cardiac antigens identified to date, providing a framework for the definition of cardiac antigens and heart specificity and a roadmap for tracking and analysing specific T cells across cardiac diseases to enable a deeper understanding of tissue-specific immune mechanisms in cardiovascular diseases.
ns1:item.dc:title: Heart-specific T cell responses: from antigens to disease mechanisms
ns1:item.dc:creator: Gustavo Campos Ramos
ns1:item.dc:source: Nature Reviews Cardiology, Published online: 2026-10-12; | doi:10.1038/s41569-026-01356-x

ns1:item.ns1:title: Beyond glucose lowering and ketogenesis: unveiling new cardioprotective mechanisms of SGLT2 inhibitors
ns1:item.ns5:encoded:
Nature Reviews Cardiology, Published online: 02 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41569-026-01357-w

Sodium–glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors improve cardiovascular outcomes in patients with heart failure (HF), but the direct cardiac effects of these drugs remain incompletely understood. Recent evidence has identified pantothenate kinase 1 (PANK1) as a direct cardiac target of SGLT2 inhibitors, whereby PANK1 activation can restore coenzyme A availability and myocardial metabolic capacity. This finding highlights the therapeutic potential of targeting the PANK1–coenzyme A axis in patients with HF.
ns1:item.dc:title: Beyond glucose lowering and ketogenesis: unveiling new cardioprotective mechanisms of SGLT2 inhibitors
ns1:item.dc:creator: Alessia Riccio
Gaetano Santulli
ns1:item.dc:source: Nature Reviews Cardiology, Published online: 2026-10-02; | doi:10.1038/s41569-026-01357-w

ns1:item.ns1:title: Global burden of venous thromboembolism: incidence and outcome estimates of deep-vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism
ns1:item.ns5:encoded:
Nature Reviews Cardiology, Published online: 27 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41569-026-01334-3

Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a major cause of morbidity and death. In this Review, Bikdeli and colleagues summarize the available evidence on the worldwide incidence and outcomes of VTE, specifically deep-vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism. Their findings reveal a substantial and, in some regions, increasing burden of disease, sources of heterogeneity and striking regional gaps in the data.

ns1:item.ns1:title: Benefit of aficamten in non-obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
ns1:item.ns5:encoded:
Nature Reviews Cardiology, Published online: 16 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41569-026-01353-0

Data from the ACACIA-HCM trial show that treatment with the myosin inhibitor aficamten improves exercise capacity and patient-reported health status compared with placebo in patients with non-obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

ns1:item.ns1:title: Tricuspid valve repair reduces death and HF hospitalization
ns1:item.ns5:encoded:
Nature Reviews Cardiology, Published online: 15 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41569-026-01351-2

In patients with symptomatic severe tricuspid regurgitation, transcatheter tricuspid repair in addition to medical therapy not only improves quality of life compared with medical therapy alone, but also significantly reduces the risk of all-cause death and hospitalization for heart failure, according to the results from the investigator-initiated TRIC-I-HF-DZHK24 trial.
ns1:item.dc:title: Tricuspid valve repair reduces death and HF hospitalization
ns1:item.dc:creator: Karina Huynh
ns1:item.dc:source: Nature Reviews Cardiology, Published online: 2026-09-15; | doi:10.1038/s41569-026-01351-2
